samples.text:
The line graph shows the average maximum and minimum temperature in a city in each month, and the bar chart shows how much rain the city get every month.

Firstly, the maximum temperature is quite stable. It is 31°C in January and goes up to 33°C in March and April, which is the highest. Then it falls to 29°C in July and August and after it increases again to 31°C in the end of year. The minimum temperature changes more. It start at 18°C in January, rises to 26°C in May and stays at 25°C from June to September.

Also, the rainfall is very different in each month. In January there is only 8mm and in December 10mm. From April the rain increases sharply and it reach the peak of 370mm in July. Then it decreases to 290mm in September and 180mm in October, and it is only 35mm in November.

Overall, the temperature is hot all year, but there is a very wet season in the middle of year and a dry season at the start and end.
samples.why: Overview is present but comes last and is basic · both charts covered with accurate figures · mechanical linking (Firstly, Then, Also) · some awkward word choice · several agreement and preposition errors.

samples.text:
The line graph illustrates the average highest and lowest temperatures in a particular city throughout the year, while the bar chart shows its average rainfall for each month.

Overall, the city is warm all year round, with maximum temperatures varying only slightly, whereas rainfall is highly seasonal, being concentrated in the middle months of the year.

Average maximum temperatures remain between 29°C and 33°C for the whole year. They peak at 33°C in March and April before dipping to a low of 29°C in July and August, and then return to 31°C for the last three months. Minimum temperatures show greater variation, climbing from 18°C in January to a high of 26°C in May. They stay at 25°C until September before falling back to 18°C in December.

In terms of rainfall, the first three months and the last two are relatively dry, with less than 50mm each month, and January is the driest at just 8mm. Rainfall rises dramatically from April onwards, reaching the peak of 370mm in July. It then declines steadily to 180mm in October and drops sharply to 35mm in November.
samples.why: Clear overview contrasting temperature and rainfall · key features highlighted with ranges and peaks · logical paragraphing · good range of vocabulary (dipping, seasonal) · mostly accurate with one minor slip.

samples.text:
The line graph compares the average monthly maximum and minimum temperatures in one city, and the bar chart presents its average monthly rainfall.

The city experiences consistently high temperatures, with the maximum fluctuating within a narrow band of just four degrees. Rainfall, by contrast, varies enormously, with a pronounced wet season from May to September and very dry conditions around the turn of the year.

Maximum temperatures are highest in March and April, at 33°C, and lowest in July and August, at 29°C, remaining between 30°C and 32°C in every other month. Minimum temperatures fluctuate more widely, from a low of 18°C in December and January to 26°C in May, and they hold steady at 25°C from June to September. As a result, the gap between the maximum and minimum is widest in December and January, at 13 degrees, and narrowest in July and August, at just four.

Rainfall is low from November to March, ranging from 8mm in January to 45mm in March. It then increases sharply, surging from 110mm in April to 260mm in May and peaking at 370mm in July. Although it falls back gradually to 290mm in September, a steep decline follows, to 180mm in October and just 35mm in November.
samples.why: Insightful overview contrasting stable temperatures with seasonal rainfall · well-chosen derived comparisons (temperature gap) · cohesion managed skilfully · precise, natural vocabulary · wide range of error-free structures.
